name: Public Scientific Data Source Registry
description: Candidate public repositories for EvidenceChain and IEVF-CORE provenance, validation, and reproducibility benchmarking. This registry intentionally separates repository metadata from validated evidence and marks dataset-specific access/version/licensing details for confirmation.

api.notes: Programmatic access is available via NCBI Entrez and GEO FTP. No single unified versioned dataset API exists for all records.

versioning.mechanism: Accession-based lineage; updates tracked through submission history
versioning.notes: Previous snapshots are not consistently exposed as formal dataset versions; dataset-specific checks are required.

access.notes: Most GEO data are public; some human-subject datasets may require controlled access (e.g., dbGaP) or study-specific approval.

license.summary: No single uniform license; submitter and repository metadata must be checked per study.

api.notes: Official REST API for experiments, files, biosamples, and metadata queries.

versioning.mechanism: Release/versioned metadata and file records; legacy records may be archived separately
versioning.notes: Versioning is handled through release metadata and file-level identity, but dataset-specific confirmation is recommended.

access.notes: Most data are public; some embargoed or limited-release records can be time-gated.

license.summary: ENCODE data is released under the Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication; confirm dataset and file-level terms if necessary.

api.notes: Public metadata and dataset access via the HCA Data Coordination Platform.

versioning.notes: Version policy is release-based and should be confirmed at the dataset or snapshot level.

access.notes: Publicly released datasets are available; some project-specific restrictions may apply.

license.summary: Data-sharing policy aligns with open publication and re-use; CC BY 4.0 is commonly referenced by HCA public resources, with dataset-specific terms to confirm.

api.notes: Official API documentation is available through the Census docs and the API is backed by the Census data model.

versioning.notes: This is one of the strongest public examples of formal versioning among scientific repositories.

access.notes: General public access; dataset-level terms must still be checked.

license.summary: Dataset-specific license metadata should be checked; general CZI materials point toward open re-use and citation-based use.

api.notes: Official PRIDE Archive REST API for dataset and file access.

versioning.mechanism: Persistent accession with dataset update history
versioning.notes: Versioning is weaker than CELLxGENE/OpenNeuro for snapshot retrieval; confirm dataset-level update policy.

access.notes: Public by default; embargo may apply until publication or release.

license.summary: PRIDE recommends open re-use and attribution; CC0 is commonly referenced, but dataset-specific conditions should be confirmed.

api.notes: Official MetaboLights API exposes study metadata and files.

versioning.notes: Formal snapshot/version retrieval should be confirmed per study and release cycle.

access.notes: Public after release or embargo policies are satisfied.

license.summary: MetaboLights is generally open and often aligns with CC0 or similar open-access principles; individual study metadata should be reviewed.

api.notes: Official API and BIDS-based public dataset access.

versioning.mechanism: Versioned dataset snapshots and immutable dataset identities
versioning.notes: OpenNeuro is one of the stronger examples of public dataset versioning through BIDS and snapshot metadata.

access.notes: Released datasets are public; sensitive or restricted data may require additional review.

license.summary: Default open re-use usually aligns with CC0; individual dataset terms should be checked.

api.notes: Official OSDR biological data API provides dataset and metadata retrieval.

versioning.notes: Formal per-dataset snapshot/version behavior should be confirmed at the record level.

access.notes: Open science repository; AWS mirror and public dataset access are intended for broad reuse.

license.summary: U.S. government research data is designed for open access; dataset-specific attribution policies should be checked.

api.notes: Official API and project documentation for materials data and structures.

versioning.mechanism: API versioning plus material record change history
versioning.notes: Project-level database snapshots and changelog metadata are available; individual material revisions should be examined when needed.

access.notes: The public API is available, but an API key is required for some access patterns and usage limits apply.

license.summary: Open materials data with CC BY-style attribution; check current documentation for exact terms.

api.notes: REST API and DOI-based dataset metadata for repository access.

versioning.mechanism: DOI and repository metadata track versions and revisions
versioning.notes: Some datasets may not expose formal snapshots; DOI metadata is the authoritative binding point.

access.notes: Most datasets are public; check individual records for embargo or exceptions.

license.summary: Many records are public domain or open-use, but dataset-specific licenses must be reviewed.

api.notes: NOAA NCEI offers multiple server interfaces for geospatial and time-series data access.

versioning.notes: Data products often maintain historical revisions; dataset-specific version metadata should be used when available.

access.notes: Public data; no user account required for most public APIs.

license.summary: U.S. government data are generally public domain; dataset-level terms may still be consulted.

api.notes: Public catalog and item retrieval API for USGS and related geospatial/scientific data.

versioning.mechanism: Catalog metadata with item revision history
versioning.notes: Versioning is not always uniform across all records; dataset-specific review is required.

access.notes: Public catalog; exceptions may apply to data with restrictions or third-party licensing.

license.summary: U.S. government public data generally carries public-domain reuse rights; dataset-specific restrictions should still be reviewed.
